set.name: Copper Echo
set.mechanism: The sonar ping that returns your own signal: one thin ring sweeps out and a single copper dot comes back — an index that answers with your collection, set in a warm listening-room dark.
set.expression_move: The copper echo dot is the only saturated moment; everything else is near-black and bone.
set.differs_by: Every competitor pairs a neutral sans with a corporate primary (Navidrome blue, Jellyfin cyan, Plex magenta, Ampache orange); this is the only warm dark room with a single deep-copper signal and a quirky grotesque.

logo.concept: A sonar sweep and its echo: the ring goes out read-only across your shelf, and the dot that comes back is your music.
logo.defect: Ring filled as two discs: the inner return arc swept the short way (wrong sweep flag), so the band resolved as a symmetric difference of two circles.

defaults_used.why: Echo Copper is the echo dot of the brand's namesake mechanism (Sonarly = sonar), not a clay or craft cue: it is a small signal on a warm dark ground, never a wash. Measured 28 CIE76 from Ampache's #f8ac4c, the only warm competitor primary — and much deeper (L* 52 vs 70), so the deep-copper signal region on the shelf is effectively unoccupied.
The ring is the sonar ping the brand is named for, not a container: it is open (60-degree gap at 3 o'clock) and carries the echo dot at its trailing end. No competitor on the shelf uses a ring mark.

rationale.claim: The measured competitor shelf is uniform: all four lead with neutral sans type (Open Sans, Noto Sans, Inter, system-ui) and blue/cyan/magenta/orange primaries, so a warm dark room with a single copper signal is unoccupied.

Echo Copper #B96A2E (L* 52.3) sits 28 CIE76 from Ampache's #f8ac4c and 35 from Plex's brand yellow — clear of the near-colour rule — and it is used as a small signal on a dark ground, not a brand wash.

Bricolage Grotesque carries display and text in one variable file (~126 KB), keeping the quiet system cheap; its I/l IoU 0.92 warning applies at small text sizes and is a known trade-off of the quirky cut.
A single-family pairing is the calmest choice and mirrors the product's boring-tech principle: one file, one voice, hierarchy from wght and opsz only.

palette.name: Copper Echo
palette.direction: A warm listening-room black, bone text, one deep-copper signal.

brand.usage: the echo dot, play state, calls to action — small signals only

set.name: Catalogue Card
set.mechanism: The collector's catalogue card: the wordmark sits on a ruled shelf line, the type is catalogue ink and slab, and one date-stamp red marks what matters — paper, ink, stamp.
set.expression_move: The stamp-red shelf rule under the wordmark, repeated as the only divider.
set.differs_by: All four competitors are dark tech products in neutral sans; this is the only light, archival direction on the shelf — it reads as the collection itself, not a streaming startup.

logo.concept: The name entered in the catalogue and set on its shelf: a slab wordmark, one red shelf rule, and a small S-on-the-rule mark for tabs and favicons.
logo.defect: Shelf rule was a guessed 440 units wide and stopped under the l, before the y; set to the full 506-unit advance so the word sits fully on its shelf.

defaults_used.why: Date-Stamp Red is a saturated library date-stamp red for small marks, not a clay or material cue: its job is the stamp, its chroma (OKLCH C 0.077) sits just under the terracotta band, and it is CIE76 52+ from every measured competitor primary.

rationale.claim: No competitor presents a light, archival direction; all four measured sites read as dark or white-techy products, so the catalogue card stands apart by ground alone.
Date-Stamp Red #C1342B is a saturated stamp red (OKLCH C 0.077, just under the terracotta band) and CIE76 52+ from every measured competitor primary.
Zilla Slab gives the catalogue a print voice, IBM Plex Mono handles figures and codes, and Public Sans keeps UI reading neutral; each family has one role.
The shelf rule under the wordmark is the set's one loud move; every other element stays quiet so the rule can repeat as the system's only divider.

set.name: Night Sweep
set.mechanism: The OLED stage at night: a thin dial track, one thick chartreuse beam sweeping it, and the dot the beam finds — wide tracked capitals on a black that stays black.
set.expression_move: The chartreuse beam is the only bright thing in the room.
set.differs_by: Jellyfin and Navidrome own friendly blues, Plex magenta, Ampache orange; none owns a phosphor lime beam on OLED black.

logo.concept: A night dial: a thin track, one thick beam sweeping it, and the dot the sweep finds — playback as the lit part of the room.
logo.defect: Track ring filled as two discs: same sweep-flag bug as set A — the inner return arc swept the short way; fixed to sweep 1. Small-mark beam also had both arc sweeps inverted.

rationale.claim: Beam Lime #C8F04B is CIE76 54+ from every measured competitor primary, and lime is vivid only at high lightness (OKLCH L 0.87) — which suits an accent that lives on dark grounds.
Funnel Display passes the tnum gate (tabular by default), so play counts and statistics stay aligned even when set in the display face.
An open track arc plus one thick beam avoids the music category's clichés (play-button triangle, equalizer bars, vinyl disc) that were named before drawing.
OLED Black #0B0D10 keeps chroma at 0.008 so the ground stays neutral black rather than navy, and the track renders in near-white on it.
